title: The month's transfers — /transfers/{YYYY-MM}.json
description:
The transfers of one locked month's shares to the listed recipients, published as their own record once they happen and linked to the month's frozen cost-support document by its hash (ops decision D64 item 1, which adopted the checked register's row 24: transfers are published as their own linked record after they happen, and the frozen file is never edited). One row per listed recipient the month's allocation gave a share to: the share as allocated, and whether it has been transferred, is held back or is still to be transferred. Once it has been transferred, the day the fees account's statement booked the transfer, its end-to-end identifier, the amount and currency it paid in the currency of the recipient's account and the rate it was converted at, its charges, the mark «Einzelauslösung» where one board member alone released it and, as soon as it has arrived, the recipient's receipt, pinned by the SHA-256 of the receipt document; while it is held back, the day it was held and a generic ground (statutes Art. 6e para. 1 item 6 and Finanzreglement § 4 Abs. 4 and 5: one line per recipient with its category, its date, its transfer charges, the Überweisungsspesen, the mark «Einzelauslösung» where one board member alone released the transfer and, as soon as it has arrived, its receipt; the charges in part, as `chargesMinor` says). The fees account's booked statement and the recipients' receipts govern what this document restates: where they and it disagree, they govern, and the divergence is a defect to report.

WHY A RECORD OF ITS OWN. The month's cost-support document (`cost-support.v1`) is the input the month lock reads, and its exact bytes are what the lock hashes: the month's ledger export publishes their SHA-256 as `batch.costSupportSha256`. Those bytes are written before the allocation exists and never change afterwards, so a document the lock froze carries `transfers: []` and cannot say who was paid. This record says it, after the transfers happen, and names that document by the same SHA-256 (`costSupportSha256`). The frozen document is never edited and never restated.

THE LINK, AND THE ARITHMETIC A READER CHECKS, stated here because JSON Schema can neither compare two documents nor sum across items, as `cost-support.v1` states its own identities: (a) `costSupportSha256` is the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the month's frozen cost-support document, and the month's ledger export carries the same value as `batch.costSupportSha256`; (b) the `transfers[]` amounts sum to that document's `passedOnMinor`, which is the export's `totals.disbursed` (`cost-support.v1` identity (4), which a document the lock froze satisfies through this record); (c) there is one row for each recipient with a `disburse` row in the month's export and no other row: its `amountMinor` is the magnitude of the sum of that recipient's `disburse` rows, and its `category` is their `categoryFundId`; (d) a row's `endToEndId` on a first attempt is the identifier the `note` of those `disburse` rows carries after `EndToEndId ` (FS07-062's ruling (c)), and every later attempt's starts with it; (e) every amount but `paidAmountMinor` is in `currency`, the frozen document's own; (f) `lockedAt` is the export's `lockedAt` to the whole second, its fraction dropped and never rounded (the export states the lock row's `createdAt` with its milliseconds; this record's instants are whole seconds, FS-00 §6.1), and no transfer is dated, and no share held, before the day of the lock in Europe/Zurich, because the allocation is locked before the transfer (statutes Art. 6a para. 4); (g) a transferred row's `chargesMinor` is the amount of the fees account's booked debit line that executed it, less the row's `amountMinor`: the `transfer-out` line that carries the row's `endToEndId` on the fees account's statement of the month the debit was booked in (`fees-account-statement.v1`). Where the frozen document carries rows of its own in `transfers[]`, as one written by hand may, this record has a row for each of them with the same recipient, category and amount, and states what became of it.

THE PATH. One document per LOCKED month with at least one executed transfer, at `/transfers/{YYYY-MM}.json` on the public data plane (FS-00 §6.2), its month in the path the way the fees account's statement has it, and like it outside `ledger/`, which the platform's index build reads as months. `jobs.index-build` renders it from the first run after one of the month's transfers is marked executed from the fees account's debit line, and never before the month's ledger export is published. A month without an executed transfer has no document. Before the month's first transfer there is nothing executed to state: the month's shares are its export's `disburse` rows. A month whose close passed nothing on never has a transfer, and its frozen document's empty `transfers[]` satisfies identity (4), with `passedOnMinor` 0, on its own.

HELD BACK (since 1.1.0). A share the Association holds back is `held` (zurückgestellt, statutes Art. 8 para. 5), with the day it was held and one generic ground, never the cause the Association's records give (ops decision D177 item 3; Finanzreglement § 9 Abs. 6 and 7): `struck (Art. 7 Abs. 6)` where its recipient was struck from the List after the month's close, whatever the ground of the striking, which the published List gives (statutes Art. 7 para. 6; never `frozen`); `transfer returned` where its transfer came back from the receiving bank (statutes Art. 6a para. 3, which sends it to Art. 8 para. 5); `account not confirmed` where the recipient's account for the transfer is not confirmed, or has changed; and `a precondition of the transfer is open` where another condition the Association's rules set for every transfer is not met yet. A share held for more than one cause shows the first of these four that applies. A held share is no transfer. A share whose transfer a prohibition of law blocks (statutes Art. 6a para. 5, «gesperrt») is shown as statutes Art. 8 para. 5 shows such an amount, held back, under the generic ground its recorded cause maps to: `struck (Art. 7 Abs. 6)` once its recipient is struck (ops decision D177 item 3). The record never says that a share is blocked, or why (Finanzreglement § 9 Abs. 6 and 7). A block that rests on no cause the records name is not stated in this version. A month withheld after its record was published keeps that document as published.

REGENERATED, NOT WRITTEN ONCE. The ledger is append-only, so a month's shares, and so its rows, are fixed from the first publication, and a row changes in five cases only: its share is transferred (`scheduled` or `held` becomes `transferred`); its transfer comes back from the receiving bank before it reached the recipient (`transferred` becomes `held` or `scheduled`, with a note saying so), so the share is owed again until it is sent again, unless its recipient is struck; the share is held back, or its hold ends (`scheduled` becomes `held`, or the reverse); an attempt of a share that is not transferred is prepared or abandoned, so the identifier its `scheduled` row carries appears, changes or goes; or the recipient's receipt arrives. `generatedAt` is derived from the records and never from a clock: its description says how, and the cases it cannot date.

NOTHING HERE NAMES A PERSON OR AN ACCOUNT. No account number or other bank detail, no bank file, no counterparty or text of a bank line, no steward, approval, cause of a hold, reason for an abandoned attempt, screening, or record of the transfer day other than the mark «Einzelauslösung» is published, and every object is closed and every reference has a fixed form, so no member can carry one; `note` carries only the producer's fixed words, and `ground` one of four. A receipt is published by its reference and the SHA-256 of its document, never its bytes: anyone can ask for a copy, which is sent with account numbers and personal data blacked out (Finanzreglement § 4 Abs. 10).

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (producer: `jobs.index-build`, from the month's `disburse` ledger rows, its transfer batches, their holds, their transfer-day checks and their receipts, platform migrations 0032 and 0087, the receipt documents' SHA-256, migration 0115, what each transfer's payment file instructed, migration 0094, the fees account's debit line of each transfer through the view of migration 0107, and the frozen cost-support document the lock read, through migration 0083's read path). No transfer has been executed on any plane yet, so no document exists outside the examples.
x-psn.artifactPath: /transfers/{YYYY-MM}.json — one per locked month with an executed transfer, unless the month is withheld
x-psn.producer: `jobs.index-build` (P-M3), from `ledger_rows` (the month's `disburse` rows), `disbursement_batches` and `disbursement_receipts` (platform migration 0032, as 0087 amended them), the holds of each share (`disbursement_holds`, 0087: the cause, never published, and the instant it was recorded), the release mode of each transfer's transfer-day checks (`transfer_day_checks`, 0087; published only as the mark «Einzelauslösung»), what each transfer's payment file instructed (`bank_file_batches`, migration 0094: the amount, its currency, the rate and the rate's day), the receipt documents' SHA-256 (`receipt_files`, migration 0115; never their bytes), the booked debit line of each transfer (the view of migration 0107: its booking date, its amount, its bank reference and the instant it was recorded) and the frozen cost-support document (`locked_cost_support_documents()`, migration 0083), whose SHA-256 it checks against the one the allocation names. No sample plane's builder renders it yet; PS-153's will
consumers: the public transparency page of each month (FS-01)
anyone checking that a month's shares reached the listed recipients (statutes Art. 12 para. 1, Art. 20 para. 1)
the annual transparency report, which aggregates months and never restates them
fsRefs: ops decision D64 item 1 (the checked register's row 24)

generatedAt.description: The document's envelope instant (FS-00 §6.2), derived from the records and never from a clock: the latest of `lockedAt`; for each transfer it shows as executed, or in a note as returned, the instant the store recorded its booked debit line (the start of its booking day where the store names no line), and the start, in Europe/Zurich, of the day of each of the recipient's receipts filed against it; the instant the store recorded each hold of the month's shares (since 1.1.0); and the instant each attempt of the month's shares was prepared, which is also the instant a hold of its share ends (since 1.1.0). So a transfer marked executed, a share held back, an attempt prepared and the end of a hold with it, or a receipt dated later than everything the document already shows, moves it past `lockedAt`. THE CASES IT CANNOT DATE: the rule takes no instant at which a transfer is marked returned or an attempt is abandoned, and it takes a receipt by its own day, never by when it was filed, so a return, an abandoned attempt, or a receipt dated before something the document already shows, changes the document without moving `generatedAt`; the bytes' ETag still changes. It is the document's own instant, not the plane's, so it differs from the `generatedAt` of the `/meta/publish-log.json` batch that lists this path whenever a newer row existed then, as the fees account's statement does.

source.description: Which plane produced this document, in the envelope's vocabulary (FS-00 §6.2): `platform` is `jobs.index-build` in `PSN_ENV=prod`, `fixture` every other environment of it, `sample` a sample plane. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane, which a production deployment refuses to serve (`sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). Required, and `registry-v0` is not admitted: the curated registry never held a transfer.

month.description: The month whose shares this record states, `YYYY-MM`: the month whose close allocated them, which is the month of the frozen cost-support document and of the ledger export, not the month the transfers are made in. It names the document's path.

lockedAt.description: The instant the month locked, as its ledger export states it (`ledger-export.v1` `lockedAt`), to the whole second: its fraction dropped and never rounded, because the export states the lock row's `createdAt` with its milliseconds and this record's instants are whole seconds (FS-00 §6.1). The lock read the frozen cost-support document and allocated the shares; every transfer comes after it.

costSupportSha256.description: THE LINK: the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the month's frozen cost-support document (`cost-support.v1`), lowercase hex, the value the month's ledger export carries as `batch.costSupportSha256`. Those bytes are never edited: this record states the transfers they cannot.

currency.description: The currency of every amount here but `paidAmountMinor` (ISO 4217): the frozen cost-support document's `currency`, which is the month's `disburse` rows' and the fees account's too. What a transfer paid in the currency of the recipient's account is `paidAmountMinor`, in `paidCurrency` (since 1.1.0).

transfers.description: One row per listed recipient that the month's allocation gave a share to (one `disburse` row or more in the month's export), and no other row: never one row per category fund, and never a row for a share of 0, which the allocation does not write (ops decision D33 item 1). Ordered by `recipientId`. Every row of the month is listed from the first publication on, transferred, held back or not yet transferred, so the amounts always sum to the frozen document's `passedOnMinor`.

instant.description: An instant in FS-00 §6.1's one spelling, UTC to the whole second, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. The pattern holds the spelling for a reader whose validator treats `format` as an annotation.

day.description: A calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. The pattern holds the spelling for a reader whose validator treats `format` as an annotation; that the day exists is `format`'s.

transfer.description: One listed recipient's share of the month and what became of it.

recipientId.description: The listed recipient, resolvable against the Recipient List version the month's export names (`batch.recipientListVersion`; `recipient-list.v1`). Money rows name organisations on the published List, never persons (URS ENG-083).

category.description: The recipient's category, the `categoryFundId` of its `disburse` rows: one of the movement's seven published categories. The closed menu is published once in `category-menu.v1` (`$defs.slug`); this contract set may not `$ref` across files, so this member constrains the vocabulary by pattern and names the published menu, as `cost-support.v1`'s transfer row does.

amountMinor.description: The recipient's share as the month's allocation gave it, in minor units of `currency`: the magnitude of the sum of the recipient's `disburse` rows of the month. Whatever its status, a row always states the share, never part of it.

status.description: `transferred`: the share's transfer was executed, as the fees account's booked debit line shows, and has not come back; the row carries its `date`, its `endToEndId`, what it paid and its charges. `held` (since 1.1.0): the Association holds the share back (zurückgestellt, statutes Art. 8 para. 5), with the day it was held (`heldOn`) and its generic ground (`ground`), never the cause its records give. `scheduled`: the share is allocated and published, the money has not reached the recipient, and nothing holds it back: it is not yet transferred, or it was transferred and came back from the receiving bank, and it is owed until it is sent again (a note then says so). A scheduled or held share is never a transfer, and no impact figure is ever drawn from one.

date.description: The day the fees account's statement booked the transfer's debit (its booking date, Europe/Zurich): the day the money left the account. Required on `transferred`, absent on `scheduled` and `held`. Never before the day of `lockedAt`.

endToEndId.description: The credit transfer's end-to-end identifier (ISO 20022 `EndToEndId`): `psn-YYYYMM-` and the last 12 characters of the recipient's ULID, where `YYYYMM` is this document's `month`, with `-n` after it for the transfer's attempt n from 2 to 9 (a transfer the bank rejected, or one that was abandoned or came back, is prepared again under the next attempt). On a first attempt it is the identifier the `note` of the recipient's `disburse` rows carries after `EndToEndId ` (FS07-062's ruling (c)), and every later attempt's starts with it. On `transferred`, required: the attempt that was executed, which the fees account's statement shows on the debit line (`fees-account-statement.v1` `endToEndId`), so a bank line and this row are matched by anyone holding both. On `scheduled`, present only while an attempt is prepared and not yet executed: the identifier it will be sent under. Never on `held`.

paidAmountMinor.description: On `transferred`, required (since 1.1.0): what the transfer paid, in minor units of `paidCurrency`, the currency of the recipient's account: the amount the Association's payment file instructed for it (ISO 20022 `InstdAmt`). Where `paidCurrency` is `currency` it is the share, `amountMinor`.

paidCurrency.description: On `transferred`, required (since 1.1.0): the currency of `paidAmountMinor` (ISO 4217), the currency of the recipient's account the transfer paid into, as the Association's payment file instructed it.

rate.description: On `transferred`, present exactly where `paidCurrency` is not `currency` (since 1.1.0): the rate the Association's payment file converted the share at, as a decimal string and never a float, the units of `paidCurrency` one unit of `currency` bought. It is the rate the European Central Bank's euro foreign exchange reference rates give, published on the bank working day before the payment file's requested execution date and crossed through the euro, and the amount paid is the share at that rate, rounded down (ops decision D177 item 2). With `rateDate`.

rateDate.description: With `rate`, and only with it (since 1.1.0): the day of the reference rate the payment file applied.

chargesMinor.description: On `transferred`, required (since 1.1.0): the transfer's charges as the fees account's statement books them on the debit line that executed it, in minor units of `currency`: the line's amount less the share (identity (g)). So it holds a charge the bank booked within the debit, and, for a transfer paid in another currency, the difference between what the conversion debited and the share, which is negative where the conversion cost less than the share: a negative conversion cost of the fees account, booked against the transfer, never income. These are the transfer's charges, the Überweisungsspesen of statutes Art. 6e para. 1 item 6 and Finanzreglement § 4 Abs. 4 and 5, as far as its debit line books them, a cost of the fees account (Cost Class Rules class 6): a charge the bank books on a line of its own is on the fees account's statement (`fees-account-statement.v1`, class `bank-charge`) and in the cost table of the month that pays it (`cost-support.v1`), and is not in this member, because the Association's records do not tie such a line to a transfer yet.

singleRelease.description: On `transferred`, present exactly where the Association's record of its transfer day states that one board member alone released the transfer (statutes Art. 19 para. 4 and 5): the mark «Einzelauslösung» (Finanzreglement § 4 Abs. 4 and 5; since 1.1.0). Absent where that record shows no single release, or holds no record of the day. The record of the transfer day is never published beyond this mark.

heldOn.description: On `held`, required, and on no other status (since 1.1.0): the day the share was held back for the cause its `ground` names, as the Association's records date that hold, in Europe/Zurich. Never before the day of `lockedAt`.

enum: a precondition of the transfer is open
ground.description: On `held`, required, and on no other status (since 1.1.0): why the share is held back, in one of four generic words and never the cause the Association's records give (ops decision D177 item 3; Finanzreglement § 9 Abs. 6 and 7). `struck (Art. 7 Abs. 6)`: the recipient was struck from the List after the month's close, whatever the ground of the striking, which the published List gives (statutes Art. 7 para. 6; never `frozen`). `transfer returned`: the share's transfer came back from the receiving bank (statutes Art. 6a para. 3 and Art. 8 para. 5). `account not confirmed`: the recipient's account for the transfer is not confirmed, or has changed. `a precondition of the transfer is open`: another condition the Association's rules set for every transfer is not met yet. Where more than one cause holds the share, the first of these four that applies.

receiptRef.description: The recipient's receipt for this transfer (ops decision D33 item 2(f)), by the `rct_` id the Association files it under, and the first of them where the recipient sent more than one: it is the `ref` of one of the row's `recipient-receipt` evidence entries. Present on a `transferred` row once the receipt has arrived and not before (Finanzreglement § 4 Abs. 5: as soon as it has arrived); never on `scheduled` or `held`.

note.description: Narrative for this row, in the producer's fixed words: for one, that the share's transfer, sent on the day it names, came back from the receiving bank and the share is owed again, unless its recipient is struck. Never an account, a person, a screening, the cause of a hold or a reason a steward wrote.

evidence.description: The documents behind a `transferred` row: the fees account's debit line, by the bank's own reference for its entry where the bank gave one, and each receipt the recipient sent for the transfer, pinned by its document's SHA-256. Absent where there is none yet, and always on `scheduled` and `held`: no transfer stands.

allOf.$comment: A transfer is published with its day, the identifier its debit line carries, what it paid and its charges, so anyone holding the fees account's statement can match the two; a share that is not transferred has none of them and no evidence, because no transfer stands.
A held share carries the day it was held and its generic ground, and no identifier: no attempt is prepared for it; no other status carries either.
A receipt reference is one of the row's receipts: a row naming a receipt carries its evidence entry, and a row carrying a receipt names one.

evidenceLink.description: One piece of evidence behind one transferred row.

kind.description: `bank-line`: the fees account's booked debit line that executed the transfer, by the bank's own reference for its entry (ISO 20022 `AcctSvcrRef`, as the fees account's statement publishes it in `bankReference`, so this entry resolves to that line's row there, or to the rows of one collective entry). `recipient-receipt`: a receipt the recipient sent for this transfer (ops decision D33 item 2(f)), by the reference the Association files it under, with its document's SHA-256.

ref.description: The evidence's own reference, which a reader can ask for by name (Finanzreglement § 4 Abs. 10): the bank's reference of the debit line's entry, in the form the fees account's statement publishes it (`fees-account-statement.v1` `bankReference`), or the receipt's `rct_` id. Each kind's form is held in `allOf` below.

sha256.description: On a `recipient-receipt` entry, and on no other: the SHA-256 of the receipt document's exact bytes, lowercase hex, so the public record pins the bytes without carrying them. A copy is sent on request with account numbers and personal data blacked out, so its own hash differs; the Association's stored document is the one this names.

allOf.$comment: A receipt is pinned by its document's hash and named by its `rct_` id; a bank line is named by the bank's reference, in the form `fees-account-statement.v1` publishes it, and carries no hash.
